title: Data Engineer
story: Cartwheel streams app events into a raw table and loads orders into a warehouse every day. You own the pipelines: cleaning, deduplication, slowly changing dimensions and incremental loads.

tables.name: events_raw
tables.about: Raw app events. Has duplicate event_id rows, missing user_id, messy event_type (case, spaces). ingested_at is when the row landed.

tables.name: customer_dim
tables.about: Type 2 slowly changing dimension: one row per customer version, valid_from to valid_to (9999-12-31 = current).

tables.name: orders_src
tables.about: Today's extract from the source system: updates to existing orders and new orders. Some rows are bad.

tasks.title: Find duplicates
tasks.question: How many rows does events_raw have, how many distinct event_ids, and how many duplicate rows? Return total_rows, distinct_events, duplicate_rows.
tasks.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rows, COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) AS distinct_events, COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) AS duplicate_rows FROM events_raw
tasks.starter:
-- Find duplicates
SELECT *
FROM events_raw
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Null audit
tasks.question: Count missing values in events_raw. Return null_user_id, null_device and null_amount.
tasks.solution:
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE user_id IS NULL) AS null_user_id, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE device IS NULL) AS null_device,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE amount IS NULL) AS null_amount FROM events_raw
tasks.starter:
-- Null audit
SELECT *
FROM events_raw
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Raw event types
tasks.question: List every raw event_type value exactly as stored with its row count. Return event_type and rows.
tasks.solution: SELECT event_type, COUNT(*) AS rows FROM events_raw GROUP BY event_type
tasks.hint: Plain GROUP BY. Notice the messy variants.
tasks.starter:
-- Raw event types
SELECT *
FROM events_raw
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Clean event types
tasks.question: Deduplicate by event_id, standardise event_type (trim + lowercase), and count events per clean type. Return event_type and events.
tasks.solution: SELECT lower(trim(event_type)) AS event_type, COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) AS events FROM events_raw GROUP BY 1
tasks.starter:
-- Clean event types
SELECT *
FROM events_raw
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Daily purchase revenue
tasks.question: Keep only the latest copy of each event_id (by ingested_at), then for purchase events (clean type) return date, purchases and revenue (sum of amount).
tasks.solution:
WITH d AS (SELECT * FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY event_id ORDER BY ingested_at DESC) AS rn FROM events_raw) WHERE rn = 1)
SELECT CAST(event_ts AS DATE) AS date, COUNT(*) AS purchases, SUM(amount) AS revenue
FROM d WHERE lower(trim(event_type)) = 'purchase' GROUP BY 1
tasks.hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY event_id ORDER BY ingested_at DESC) = 1 keeps the latest.
tasks.starter:
-- Daily purchase revenue
SELECT *
FROM events_raw
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Ingestion lag
tasks.question: Average lag in minutes between event_ts and ingested_at per device, with missing device shown as unknown. Return device and avg_lag_min (2 decimals), using all raw rows.
tasks.solution:
SELECT COALESCE(device, 'unknown') AS device, ROUND(AVG(date_diff('second', event_ts, ingested_at)) / 60.0, 2) AS avg_lag_min
FROM events_raw GROUP BY 1
tasks.starter:
-- Ingestion lag
SELECT *
FROM events_raw
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Point-in-time lookup
tasks.question: Using customer_dim, how many customers lived in each city on 2023-09-01? A version is valid when valid_from <= date < valid_to. Return city and customers.
tasks.solution:
SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customer_dim
WHERE valid_from <= DATE '2023-09-01' AND valid_to > DATE '2023-09-01'
GROUP BY city
tasks.hint: Filter versions that cover the date, then group.
tasks.starter:
-- Point-in-time lookup
SELECT *
FROM customer_dim
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Customers who moved
tasks.question: How many customers changed city at least once across their versions? Return one value: customers.
tasks.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM customer_dim GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT city) > 1)
tasks.starter:
-- Customers who moved
SELECT *
FROM customer_dim
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Incremental upsert
tasks.question: Merge orders_src into orders_wh by order_id: new orders are inserted; existing orders take the source row only if src.updated_at is newer. Ignore source rows with amount <= 0. Return status and orders after the merge.
tasks.solution:
WITH s AS (SELECT * FROM orders_src WHERE amount > 0),
m AS (
  SELECT w.order_id, CASE WHEN s.order_id IS NOT NULL AND s.updated_at > w.updated_at THEN s.status ELSE w.status END AS status FROM orders_wh w LEFT JOIN s USING (order_id)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT s.order_id, s.status FROM s WHERE s.order_id NOT IN (SELECT order_id FROM orders_wh))
SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM m GROUP BY status
tasks.hint: Update existing rows with a LEFT JOIN + CASE, then UNION ALL the new ones.
tasks.starter:
-- Incremental upsert
SELECT *
FROM orders_wh
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Change data capture
tasks.question: Classify each orders_src row as insert (order not in warehouse), update (exists and status or amount differs) or no change. Return change_type and rows.
tasks.solution:
SELECT CASE WHEN w.order_id IS NULL THEN 'insert' WHEN s.status <> w.status OR s.amount <> w.amount THEN 'update' ELSE 'no change' END AS change_type,
       COUNT(*) AS rows
FROM orders_src s LEFT JOIN orders_wh w USING (order_id) GROUP BY 1
tasks.hint: LEFT JOIN source to target and test the columns.
tasks.starter:
-- Change data capture
SELECT *
FROM orders_wh
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Sessionise events
tasks.question: Deduplicate by event_id and drop rows without user_id. Sort each user's events by event_ts; a new session starts when the gap from the previous event is more than 30 minutes (or it is the user's first event). How many sessions are there? result: one number.
tasks.solution:
d = events_raw.drop_duplicates('event_id').dropna(subset=['user_id']).copy()
d['ts'] = pd.to_datetime(d['event_ts'])
d = d.sort_values(['user_id', 'ts'])
gap = d.groupby('user_id')['ts'].diff()
result = int((gap.isna() | (gap > pd.Timedelta(minutes=30))).sum())
tasks.hint: groupby('user_id')['ts'].diff() gives the gap to the previous event.
tasks.starter:
# Sessionise events
# DataFrames ready: events_raw, customer_dim, orders_wh, orders_src
# Put your final answer in a variable called result
result = events_raw.head()

result = c['tier'].value_counts().rename_axis('tier').rename('customers')

tasks.title: Validate the extract
tasks.question: Before loading orders_src, count rows breaking each rule: negative_amount (amount <= 0) and stale_update (order exists in orders_wh and src updated_at is not newer). result: rule and failed.
tasks.solution:
m = orders_src.merge(orders_wh[['order_id', 'updated_at']], on='order_id', how='left', suffixes=('', '_wh'))
stale = m['updated_at_wh'].notna() & (m['updated_at'] <= m['updated_at_wh'])
result = pd.DataFrame({'rule': ['negative_amount', 'stale_update'], 'failed': [int((orders_src.amount <= 0).sum()), int(stale.sum())]})
tasks.hint: Left merge the warehouse timestamps in and compare.
